html:
SMTO-SSH-0003 — SMTO's saved record of this SSH connection is damaged

GUID: b9869478-3792-4695-b304-11c046422e6e
Slug: ssh-revision-invalid
Domain: SSH · Subsystem: ssh

What happened

  • SMTO keeps a check code with each SSH connection it remembers, so it can tell when the details change. That code was missing or malformed, so SMTO wouldn't reuse the saved details.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Before running the command again, check whether it already did its job on the remote computer, for example whether the file was created or the service restarted. SMTO checks this record around the time the command runs, so the command may already have finished.
  2. Start a new conversation by typing /new and ask SMTO to run the SSH command there if it still needs to run. A new conversation doesn't carry the damaged record and creates a fresh one after the next successful connection.
  3. If the same message appears in the new conversation, select Copy error details in this panel. A freshly created record should always be valid, so a repeat points to a problem inside SMTO.

What success looks like

  • The SSH command runs in the new conversation, and later SSH commands there reuse the connection without this message.

If it still fails

  • Send the copied error details to the person who manages SMTO. Don't type or paste a check code yourself; SMTO must create it from a real connection.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A remembered SSH setup carried a config_revision that is not a 64-character lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 digest.

What this means

  • validate_public requires config_revision to match a 64-character lowercase hexadecimal digest and rejects any other representation. Continuity evidence and command outcome are separate. Only the explicit pre-dispatch privilege refusal proves no new execution; observation failure alone cannot prove that a prior SSH command had no effect.

Why this can happen

  • validate_public requires config_revision to match a 64-character lowercase hexadecimal digest and rejects any other representation.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the revision shape; this check alone does not prove a well-formed revision is current.

How to fix it

  • validate_public rejects a config_revision that is not exactly 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters; the value is the SHA-256 of the alias/host/port/user/config_ref mapping computed by Observation._setup. Do not hand-edit or fabricate it; refresh by re-enrolling from a successful verified ssh run (for example in a new conversation), and report it if a freshly enrolled setup is rejected.
  • Refresh supported SSH discovery and use its returned revision without fabricating one.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • A fresh supported observation supplies the revision associated with the intended configuration.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • Continuity evidence and command outcome are separate. Only the explicit pre-dispatch privilege refusal proves no new execution; observation failure alone cannot prove that a prior SSH command had no effect.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
